method: individual review: the source window of every examined record was read; a record was closed only where a contract (comment, docstring, schema note, declared type/setter, caller return contract, or an in-block domain rule) governs the construct
note: each record documents one or more ledger items at the same site; closures are counted per ledger item, not per record

records.items: ledger items at tabs/w5_Equipment_Widget.py:771 and 772 (R-EXC-PASS, R-PASS-EXC)
records.evidence_kind: code comment states a security contract that the handler does not enforce
records.evidence: "Read-only roles must never mutate equipment/inventory, regardless of whether the control happens to be enabled (Gate Q). Backend persistence is the authority, not UI widget state." (lines 757-759) surrounding the try/except at 762-772
records.reasoning: if the permission lookup itself raises, the handler passes and the function continues towards persistence — a fail-open on a gate the file calls authoritative; canonical pattern elsewhere is a direct module-level import (16 sites, only 3 inside a try), so this outlier needs the security owner's ruling
records.question: on permission-control failure, must saving be denied (fail-closed) or is continuing the intended behaviour?
records.missing_fact: whether the permission lookup can raise in production (core/permissions.py failure modes) and the intended fail direction
records.why_it_matters: a silent control failure would let a read-only role mutate data the file says must never be mutated
